chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi'a, linking it up through his chain to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

He said: There are seven places/times in which there is no specific (time-bound) supplication: the funeral prayer, Qunut, Al-Mustajar, Safa and Marwa, standing at Arafat, and the two units of the circumambulation prayer.

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةُ: Safa and Marwa (the hills between which pilgrims walk)
key_terms.الْوُقُوفُ بِعَرَفَاتٍ: Standing at Arafat (a key ritual of Hajj)
key_terms.رَكْعَتَا الطَّوَافِ: The two units of circumambulation prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the seven occasions in Shia Islam where specific time-bound supplications are not required?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies seven specific ritual contexts where a fixed, obligatory supplication is not mandated, highlighting the flexibility of devotional practice in these moments. These contexts include the funeral prayer, Qunut, Istijar, the Sa'i between Safa and Marwa, standing at Arafat, and the two rak'ahs of Tawaf. This narration underscores the distinction between obligatory acts of worship and recommended supplications within Shia jurisprudence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-42 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma’il ibn Bazi’a who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB),

“It is not necessary to make any especial supplications in seven instances: prayer for a deceased one, Qunut in the Al-Mustajar ; Safa and Marva; Arafat and in the two units of circumambulations prayer.”
